audit.whatIsWrong: Insanity Potion is described purely as a stat buff — 'floods Singed with move speed and resistances', 'gives him a massive stat burst' — and its Grievous Wounds is never mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds. Against Tahm Kench specifically that is the whole matchup: his kit is two healing effects, Tongue Lash's heal on champion hit and Thick Skin's out-of-combat grey-health recovery, and standing in the trail under his ultimate halves both. The entry has him losing to move speed, which is the cosmetic half of the problem. The important nuance is that Grievous Wounds cuts healing, not shielding — the Thick Skin active still converts stored damage into a full-value shield under it. So the correct adjustment is to stop idling out of combat to heal grey health and start spending it as a shield instead, which is a completely different way to play the ultimate window and appears nowhere.
audit.corrected: From 6, his Poison Trail carries Grievous Wounds and halves both your heals. Grey health you were saving to idle back is worth nothing — press Thick Skin and take the shield, which anti-heal does not touch.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Adhesive appears zero times in the entry. Singed's W is entirely absent from a matchup write-up that covers his P, Q, E and R.
audit.why: Mega Adhesive is a 1000-range thrown zone that slows and grounds. Grounding shuts off movement abilities, which means Abyssal Dive — Tahm Kench's only gap-closer and only disengage — cannot be cast while he is standing in it. It is also half of Singed's kill combo: Fling a target into the goo and they are rooted rather than merely displaced. A Tahm Kench who does not know the goo exists will walk into it, find his W greyed out, and be flung and rooted with no idea why.
audit.corrected: Mega Adhesive grounds you: no Abyssal Dive in or out while you stand in it, and a Fling that lands you in it roots you outright. It is 17 seconds at rank 1 — the single cooldown worth counting in this lane.
sources: champ-data/_kits/singed.json (W Mega Adhesive, flags.grounding 'shuts off enemy dashes')

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this entry with 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and it is accurate — there is not one real number and not one wait-for-X-then-Y line in the whole matchup.
audit.why: The numbers exist and they are decisive. Fling is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8 at 125 range, so Singed has to be in melee to use it and it is down for ten seconds afterwards. Mega Adhesive is 17/16/15/14/13. Those two are the only things in his kit that can stop a Tahm Kench from closing, and once both are spent he is a champion with no CC standing next to a stun.
audit.corrected: Wait for the goo to be thrown and Fling to be spent, then walk in — that is a ten-second window with nothing in his kit to stop the third stack, the stun and the Devour.

audit.why: The knockup-enabler row in _missing-interactions.json is sound for this pairing, unlike the Rumble one — Fling genuinely knocks up and Abyssal Dive genuinely knocks up, so the displacement race is real. The entry already treats Fling as an interrupt on your commit, so I added the mirror rather than restating it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tahm Kench's W is called 'Abyssal Voyage' in spikes[2], mid, late, whys[3] and whys[6], and is used as a global rotation tool ('use Abyssal Voyage globally', 'global pressure via Abyssal Voyage').
audit.why: The live W is Abyssal Dive, 1000-1200 range with a knockup, from level 2. It is not global. Worse, in this specific matchup it is the ability Singed's Mega Adhesive turns off — so the entry names it wrongly, scales it wrongly, and misses the one interaction that matters for it.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive (W), 1000-1200 knockup, and it is disabled while you are grounded by Mega Adhesive.

edits.before: From levels 4-5 Singed starts becoming genuinely slippery — his base move speed compounds with his passive resistance stacking and you have no ultimate to close distance if he kites you around a minion wave. Stop chasing and farm; your Thick Skin grey health is doing real work absorbing incidental trail contact, but only if you activate E and step out of combat before he can re-engage. Level 6 does not fix this lane — Insanity Potion turns him into a runaway drain-tank who out-resistances your short-trade damage and cannot be caught without blowing Flash. Use Abyssal Voyage to impact other lanes rather than burning resources trying to kill a Singed who simply runs faster than you can follow.
edits.after: From levels 4-5 Singed gets genuinely slippery, but the ability that beats you is Mega Adhesive, not his boots: standing in it grounds you, and grounded means Abyssal Dive will not cast at all. It is 17 seconds at rank 1 and Fling is 10 — wait for both, then walk in, because nothing else in his kit stops a third stack. Level 6 changes the maths again: Insanity Potion makes his Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds, halving Tongue Lash's heal and Thick Skin's grey-health recovery. Inside the trail, stop idling to heal and press E for the shield, which anti-heal does not reduce. Remember the two abilities chain: a Fling that drops you into the goo roots you outright, so respect them as one combo.

edits.before: Singed with Rylai's and Liandry's is doing unavoidable sustained damage through poison-slow fields your grey health cannot regenerate fast enough to outlast, especially in extended side-lane skirmishes where he controls the geometry. Your job shifts to wave-clear parity and global pressure via Abyssal Voyage — escort your carries, use Devour to peel their engage, and let your team's composition deal with him rather than committing your own resources to a 1v1 you cannot cleanly win. If you catch him with a Flash-Q stun into Devour you can create a kill window, but burning Flash on Singed in the side lane when your team needs you is rarely the right call.

Your job shifts to wave-clear parity and peeling — escort your carries, use Devour on their engage, and refuse the side-lane 1v1 on his ground, where he picks the geometry and you fight through permanent anti-heal. If you do take it, fight outside the trail and outside the goo: on clean ground your Abyssal Dive is live, his Fling is a ten-second cooldown, and the stun into Devour is real.

notes: This matchup was flagged in the packet for having no cooldown sequencing anywhere and that was correct — but the bigger problem was that Mega Adhesive appeared zero times in the entry. Singed's W was simply not in the write-up, despite being the ability that grounds Tahm Kench out of his only gap-closer and the second half of the Fling root combo. Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds was likewise absent, described only as 'move speed and resistances', in a matchup against a champion who is entirely built out of two healing effects. The Grievous-Wounds-cuts-healing-but-not-shields distinction is the one claim here I would rate Medium rather than High: it is the standard behaviour of the debuff, but the Tahm Kench kit's needsResearch block is empty by design, so nothing on disk confirms how Thick Skin's active is treated. Worth a wiki check before this ships.
